newsitem.title: USA: Dole to shrink dried fruit, nut business.
newsitem.headline: Dole to shrink dried fruit, nut business.

text.p: Dole Food Co. Inc. said Monday it will shrink its money-losing dried fruit and nut business and take a fourth-quarter restructuring charge of about $50 million.
Dole's stock fell sharply on the news, losing $3.875 to $31.875 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Dole, the world's largest producer and marketer of fresh fruit and vegetables, said the move will remove sizable losses associated with the business and reduce its working capital substantially.
Dole said the move is part of its previously announced plan to dispose of assets that do not meet the Westlake Village, Calif.-based company's minimum return on investment requirement.

Dole also said it expects fourth-quarter earnings to more than double over the year-ago period, despite poor market conditions in the European Union and floods that have affected operations in Guatemala and Honduras.
Dole, which markets a growing line of packaged food, had 1995 revenue of $3.8 billion.
